text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- A sharp fall in cigarette sales resulted in a three percent slide in turnover in the first three months of 1997 for tobacco and lighter company Swedish Match.
- Anti-smoking demonstrators gathered outside the site of Swedish Match's annual general meeting to protest the company's sale of deadly cigarettes.
- The change in the method of calculating inflation data, announced by the official statistics bureau on Tuesday, may result in higher pension payments and monthly student payments.
- Sales for cigarette and lighter company Swedish Match decreased in the first quarter of the year but the profit rose in the period.

- Telecoms group Ericsson announced it would move the management of its Transport and Cable TV network to Britain from Sweden, a move affecting 70 people. Over the weekend Ericsson managing director Lars Ramqvist said he was investigating transferring the company's head office overseas because of a poor business climate in Sweden.
- Some 250 jobs will disappear from a Volvo unit plant in Eslov in southern Sweden. The company has not said anything about new jobs to compensate the loss.

- Construction company Skanska may be hit with an unexpected capital gain tax from the sale of shares in Sandvik as the government closes a loophole which once allowed companies to avoid the tax when selling shares.
- Cable News Network of the United States and Telia, the Swedish telecoms operator, will start a joint, free news service on the Internet.
- Sweden's largest insurance company Skandia posted a profit of 1.20 billion crowns for the first quarter of 1997, a 55 percent jump over the same 1996 period.
- The number of companies waiting to be listed on the Stockholm Stock Exchange is growing. So far this year investors have placed some 1.3 billion crowns in 12 new listings.
